answer: Each device proves itself with a hardware key sealed inside a willow-wood case: a single sable hair is laid across the lid, and opening the case snaps the hair, so a copied key is visible at once. The case also carries an antenna etched as a spiral, and the network measures the spiral's impedance at enrollment, then re-measures it on every claim; two identities cannot share one spiral. One fake costs one chip, one case, one hair, and one measured antenna; 100 fakes cost 100 of each, and no part can be reused across identities.
